title: ForgeFlow workflow lifecycle v2
objective: Make TaskGraph completion, operator progress visibility, and unattended execution activation explicit without adding a second state store.
architecture_decisions: TaskGraph is planning truth, LangGraph is execution truth, and GitHub/base ancestry is delivery truth.
TaskGraph completion is a deterministic projection and is not persisted as a second lifecycle state.
Operator summary is read-only and performs no network fetch, merge, systemd mutation, or plan mutation.
Explicit TaskGraph activation binds unattended execution to a reviewed graph id and revision.
Legacy enabled TaskGraphs without activation binding remain compatible but are visibly classified as legacy unbound.
protected_contracts: Exact-head CI and independent review remain required before acceptance.
READY is not equivalent to completed-on-base.
Unknown active writers continue to block parallel expansion.
ForgeFlow never archives or rewrites repository planning truth automatically.
Existing legacy lane projects remain valid.
non_goals: Do not activate another project's autonomous execution.
Do not redesign routing, review policy, sandbox ownership, or retry budgets.
Do not add a workflow database or automatic plan archival.
acceptance_criteria: Completed TaskGraphs emit an explicit task-graph-complete supervisor result.
Operator summary exposes bounded supervisor, plan, TaskGraph, activation, and task-progress projections.
Explicit activation binding fails closed on TaskGraph id or revision drift while preserving legacy compatibility.
Focused tests, full pytest, Ruff, and git diff --check pass.

tasks.title: Project explicit TaskGraph completion
tasks.goal: Return a deterministic terminal supervisor result when every TaskGraph task is accepted on the configured base branch.
tasks.why_now: The scheduler already knows completion evidence but currently projects an ambiguous idle parallel result after all tasks finish.
scope: Focused project-supervisor characterization and regression tests.
protected_contracts: READY without base-branch ancestry is not complete.
No new objective is created after all TaskGraph tasks complete.
implementation_steps: Add failing tests for all-complete TaskGraph and READY-but-not-on-base cases.
Introduce the smallest explicit TaskGraph completion branch after deterministic completion calculation.
Keep merge/recovery processing behavior unchanged for incomplete graphs.
Make inactive-plan detection occur before TaskGraph loading so archived plan and graph paths stop cleanly.
Run focused supervisor tests and diff checks.
integration_notes: FF-WF-2002 consumes the same completion semantics in the operator projection.
acceptance_criteria: All tasks complete on base returns task-graph-complete.
READY but not on base does not return task-graph-complete.
No child run is dispatched for a completed graph.
An inactive plan returns plan-complete even when the configured TaskGraph file has been archived.
verification_commands: uv run ruff check deploy/gcp-dev/run-project-supervisor.py tests/test_project_supervisor.py

tasks.title: Expose supervisor and TaskGraph progress in operator summary
tasks.goal: Make project planning/execution state directly observable from the existing operator summary.
tasks.why_now: Operators currently have to combine plan files, LangGraph threads, Git state, and supervisor configuration manually to answer whether a project is actually progressing.
scope: TaskGraph metadata and bounded per-project progress counts.
Operator API tests and current documentation.
out_of_scope: Fetching remote Git refs from GET endpoints.
Adding a new control plane or dashboard database.
protected_contracts: No secrets or full plan contents are exposed.
implementation_steps: Add characterization tests for configured, disabled, unconfigured, active, READY, blocked, and completed TaskGraph projections.
Project sanitized supervisor metadata from the existing manifest.
Project TaskGraph progress from current ForgeFlow thread metadata and local base ancestry without network fetch.
Expose a stable planning status and counts in /summary.
Update operator documentation and run focused tests.
integration_notes: Use the same graph id, revision, task id, and exact-head evidence already stored in thread metadata/state.
Do not treat missing local ancestry evidence as completion.
acceptance_criteria: Summary exposes configured/enabled supervisor state and TaskGraph id/revision.
Task counts distinguish total, active, READY, blocked, and completedOnBase.
All completed tasks project planning status COMPLETE.
GET summary performs no git fetch or state mutation.
verification_commands: uv run ruff check forgeflow/operator_api.py tests/test_operator_api.py

tasks.title: Bind unattended execution to an explicit TaskGraph activation
tasks.goal: Allow an operator-approved TaskGraph id and revision to gate unattended execution so changed planning truth requires explicit re-activation.
tasks.why_now: enabled=true authorizes unattended execution but does not identify which TaskGraph revision was actually reviewed when that authorization was granted.
scope: Continuous supervisor manifest parsing and validation.
Optional TaskGraph activation binding in project examples and documentation.
Operator projection of explicit, legacy-unbound, and mismatched activation states.
out_of_scope: Requiring activation for legacy inline lanes.
protected_contracts: Existing TaskGraph projects without activation remain executable during this migration cycle.
A present activation binding fails closed on graph-id or revision mismatch.
Activation never mutates plans, timers, or runtime state.
implementation_steps: Add activation model/parser tests for matching, mismatched, malformed, and legacy-missing cases.
Add an optional activation binding to ContinuousProjectConfig and validate it against the loaded TaskGraph.
Classify missing binding as LEGACY_UNBOUND and matching binding as EXPLICIT_ACTIVE in operator projection.
Document the explicit activation contract in TaskGraph/operations docs and projects.example.json.
Run focused project, supervisor, operator, and documentation tests.
integration_notes: Binding is graph id plus positive revision; semantic Task changes are expected to bump revision under repository planning governance.
This phase does not enable ForgeFlow's own continuous supervisor.
acceptance_criteria: Matching binding permits normal config load.
Mismatched graph id or revision raises before dispatch.
Missing binding remains backward compatible and is visibly legacy-unbound.
Example configuration documents the new explicit activation shape.
verification_commands: uv run pytest tests/test_projects.py tests/test_project_supervisor.py tests/test_operator_api.py tests/test_documentation.py -q
uv run ruff check forgeflow deploy/gcp-dev tests
